questions.question: Write the measurement variables of Ecological Footprint.
questions.solution_html:
• Ecological Footprint measures human demand on nature through variables such as
  • cropland, grazing land, forest area, fishing grounds, built -up land, and carbon footprint -
  • representing the biologically productive area needed to sustain resource consumption.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the role of sustainable agriculture in the NAPCC.
questions.solution_html:
• National Action Plan on Climate Change ( NAPCC) promotes sustainable agriculture
  • through efficient irrigation, soil health management, crop diversification, and climate-resilient
  • farming practices- aiming to enhance productivity while reducing emissions and preserving
  • ecological balance.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the constitutional challenges in implementing environmental laws in India
questions.solution_html:
• Constitutional challenges include overlapping jurisdictions, weak enforcement, limited
  • awareness- conflict between fundamental rights and development priorities - hindering
  • effective implementation of environmental laws in India.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Examine the impact of climate change on agriculture in developing countries.
questions.solution_html:
• Climate change affects agriculture in developing countries by altering rainfall patterns,
  • increasing droughts, reducing yields, and threatening food security- worsening poverty and
  • livelihood dependence on natural resources.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write a short essay on the purpose of the National Clean Energy Program.
questions.solution_html:
• National Clean Energy Program aims to promote renewable energy sources like solar and
  • wind, reduce carbon emissions, and achieve energy security- promoting sustainable economic
  • development in India.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the eco-centric aspect of Deep Ecology.
questions.solution_html:
• Deep Ecology emphasizes intrinsic value of all living beings - advocating an eco -centric
  • worldview that prioritizes ecological balance, biodiversity preservation - coexistence over
  • human-cantered development and exploitation.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Analyse the role of Earth Summit 1992 in balancing economic growth and environmental protection.
questions.solution_html:
• Earth Summit 1992 promoted sustainable development by introducing Agenda 21 and Rio
  • Declarations-encouraging nations to integrate environmental protection with economic
  • growth and global cooperation.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the role of Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in promoting environmental protection through Supreme Court judgments.
questions.solution_html:
• Public Interest Litigation allows citizens to approach the Supreme Court for environmental
  • protection, leading to landmark judgments -Ganga pollution and Vellore case - reinforcing
  • environmental rights under Article 21.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the concept of “climate justice.”
questions.solution_html:
• Climate justice links human rights with climate action - emphasizing that those least
  • responsible for emissions often face the worst impacts - demanding fairness, equity, and
  • accountability in global climate policies.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the role of organic farming in the Farm to Fork Strategy. [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Organic farming in the Farm to Fork Strategy reduces chemical use, promotes biodiversity,
  • ensures soil health, and supports sustainable food systems -supported by an Organic Action
  • Plan- helping the EU achieve environmental and health goals by 2030.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Analyse how public trust doctrine balances economic development with environmental conservation.
questions.solution_html:
• Public trust doctrine ensures that natural resources like air, water, and forests are held in
  • trust by the state for public use-prevents overexploitation by private or governmental entities,
  • promoting a balance between economic development and environmental conservation
  • through responsible, sustainable use of shared resources.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the key recommendations and principles adopted at the Stockholm Conference.
questions.solution_html:
• 1972 Stockholm Conference emphasized the right to a healthy environment and the
  • responsibility to protect i t-recommended integrating environmental concerns into
  • development planning, controlling pollution, conserving resources- promoting international
  • cooperation-26 principles adopted laid the foundation for global environmental governance
  • and sustainable development policies.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the penalties and punishments provided under the Environment Protection Act, 1986. Do you think they are sufficient to prevent environmental violations?
questions.solution_html:
• Environment Protection Act, 1986 prescribes imprisonment up to five years or fines up to
  • one lakh rupees for violations, with higher penalties for continued offences -provides a
  • deterrent framework, weak enforcement, bureaucratic delay s-inadequate monitoring often
  • limits its effectiveness in preventing recurring environmental violations.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Examine the causes and consequences of ozone layer depletion and discuss the international efforts to address it. [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Ozone layer depletion is caused mainly by chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and halons, leading
  • to harmful UV radiation, health risks, and ecological imbalance -international efforts like the
  • Vienna Convention (1985) and Montreal Protocol (1987) successfully phased out ozone -
  • depleting substances, showing effective global cooperation in addressing environmental
  • challenges through policy and technology shifts.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
